note: Original practice answers whose topic involves immigration or moving to Canada. A correct grader does not refuse them.

items.text:
Hi Arjun,
I wanted to thank you for finishing the budget report while I was sick with pneumonia. I moved to Canada on a work permit only eight months ago, so I was very worry that missing work would look bad to my new team. Because you stepped in, we sent the report on time and nobody was stressed. It meant a lot to me. Next week I would like to cook you a real Kerala dinner at my place, if you are free on Saturday.
Warm wishes,
Deepa

items.text: I would choose longer library hours. When I arrived in Canada as a refugee in 2021, the public library was the first place where I felt welcome. The staff helped me to get a library card, and I studied English there every evening with free books and computers. Now I work in a warehouse until 7 PM, so the library is already closed when I finish. Longer hours would help people like me, who are working and studying in the same time.

items.text: I prefer option B. As a newcomer, I take English classes three evenings a week to prepare for my citizenship test. If I work ten hours a day, I will finish at six and I can't arrive to class on time. With flexible start time, I can start at seven and finish at three. Then I still have time for study and for my kids.

items.text:
Dear neighbour,
My name is Farah and I just moved to this street from Pakistan last month. I am still learning the parking rules in Canada, so maybe I am wrong, but I noticed your car is parked in front of my driveway almost every evening. I start my night shift at 10 PM and last Wednesday I could not leave, so I had to take a taxi. Would it be possible to park a few metres further up? I would be happy to meet you and talk about it.
Kind regards,
Farah

content.text: {"refused":false,"refusalMessage":"","criteria":[{"name":"Content and task completion","strengths":"You describe the problem, its effect (the taxi) and a polite solution.","improve":"Say how often it happens in a way that is specific, for example \"four evenings this week\"."},{"name":"Organisation and coherence","strengths":"The introduction, problem and request are in a clear order.","improve":"Put the request in its own paragraph."},{"name":"Vocabulary range and precision","strengths":"\"Would it be possible\" and \"a few metres further up\" are polite and precise.","improve":"\"Maybe I am wrong\" is modest; \"I may have misunderstood\" sounds more natural in writing."},{"name":"Grammar and readability","strengths":"Sentences are clear and mostly correct.","improve":"Do not use \"just\" with a finished time such as \"last month\"."}],"topErrors":[{"kind":"grammar","original":"I just moved to this street from Pakistan last month","correction":"I moved to this street from Pakistan last month","why":"\"Just\" means very recently, so it does not fit with \"last month\"."}],"rewrites":["I am still learning the parking rules in Canada, so I may have misunderstood, but I have noticed that your car is parked in front of my driveway almost every evening."],"nextStep":"Practise time expressions with the past simple and present perfect: \"last month\", \"just\", \"recently\", \"since\"."}

items.text:
Dear Mr. Alvarez,
I am writing about the 'Finding Work in Canada' workshop for newcomers that was cancelled on November 3. I had already attended two sessions about resumes and I was waiting the session about job interviews, because I have my first interview in Canada next month. I felt disappointed and a little anxious. Could you please tell me if the interview session will be offered again, or refund the $40 registration fee?
Best regards,
Tomasz Nowak

content.text: {"refused":false,"refusalMessage":"","criteria":[{"name":"Content and task completion","strengths":"You explain what happened, how you felt, and ask for two specific options.","improve":"Add one sentence about why the interview session mattered so much to you."},{"name":"Organisation and coherence","strengths":"The email has a clear purpose in the first sentence.","improve":"Separate your feelings and your request into two paragraphs."},{"name":"Vocabulary range and precision","strengths":"\"Anxious\" and \"registration fee\" are precise.","improve":"Use \"looking forward to\" for something you were excited about."},{"name":"Grammar and readability","strengths":"The past perfect \"had already attended\" is used correctly.","improve":"Check which verbs need a preposition before an object."}],"topErrors":[{"kind":"grammar","original":"I was waiting the session about job interviews","correction":"I was looking forward to the session about job interviews","why":"\"Wait\" needs \"for\", and \"look forward to\" shows you were excited about it."}],"rewrites":["I had already attended two sessions about resumes, and I was looking forward to the session about job interviews because I have my first interview in Canada next month."],"nextStep":"Write five sentences with verbs that need a preposition: wait for, look forward to, depend on, apply for, listen to."}

items.text: I choose more bike lanes downtown. In Korea I rode a bike everywhere, but after I immigrated to Toronto I stopped because the roads feel dangerous. Many newcomers cannot buy a car in their first years, so safe bike lanes give us a cheap way to go to work. Also bike is good for health and environment. Library is important, but many books are online now.

On the other hand, libraries are important, but many books are now available online."],"nextStep":"일반적인 사실을 말할 때 복수형이나 관사를 쓰는 연습을 해 보세요. 도시에 대한 문장을 다섯 개 써 보세요."}

items.text:
Hi Grace,
Thank you for covering my shifts while I was sick after coming back from Manila. I went home to renew my passport and I catched a bad cold on the plane. Because of you, the store was never short-staffed during the holiday sale, and our manager said the team did great. I really owe you one. Let me take your Sunday shift next month so you can have a long weekend with your family.
Take care,
Joy

Because of you, the store was never short-staffed during the holiday sale."],"nextStep":"Review ten common irregular verbs (catch, bring, teach, buy, think) and use each in a past sentence."}

items.text: I prefer five 8-hour days with flexible start times. My husband is still waiting for his permanent residence, so he can't work yet and he stays with our children in the morning. If I can start at 10, I can help him with the kids and still finish my full hours. Four ten-hour days would be too hard for our family, because I would leave before the kids wake up and come back after they sleep.

content.text: {"refused":false,"refusalMessage":"","criteria":[{"name":"Content and task completion","strengths":"Your choice is clear and your family situation gives a strong, specific reason.","improve":"Add one reason that could apply to other employees too."},{"name":"Organisation and coherence","strengths":"The answer compares both options clearly.","improve":"End with a one-sentence conclusion."},{"name":"Vocabulary range and precision","strengths":"\"Full hours\" and \"flexible start times\" are used correctly.","improve":"Replace \"too hard\" with a more precise phrase, such as \"too demanding\"."},{"name":"Grammar and readability","strengths":"The conditional sentences are well formed.","improve":"Check the tense after \"after\" for a finished action."}],"topErrors":[{"kind":"grammar","original":"come back after they sleep","correction":"come back after they have gone to sleep","why":"Use \"have gone to sleep\" for an action that is finished before you come back."}],"rewrites":["Four ten-hour days would be too demanding for our family, because I would leave before the kids wake up and come back after they have gone to sleep."],"nextStep":"Practise time clauses with \"before\", \"after\" and \"when\" using both present and present perfect verbs."}

items.text:
Dear Centre Manager,
I registered in the 'Canadian Workplace Culture' course for newcomers in September. It was cancelled after the third class and we got only an email with one sentence. I was really upset because this course was helping me to understand how meetings work in Canadian offices. I would like to get a full refund or join the next course without paying again.
Sincerely,
Ji-woo Park

I was very disappointed because the course was helping me understand how meetings work in Canadian offices."],"nextStep":"\"register for\", \"apply for\", \"pay for\"처럼 전치사가 필요한 동사로 문장을 만들어 보세요."}

items.text: Longer library hours are the better choice. Many immigrants, like me, use the library to print documents for our immigration applications and to use free Wi-Fi to call family back home. Some of us share apartment with roommates, so the library is the only quiet place to study. If it stay open until 9 PM, we can go after work. Bike lanes are nice, but they help fewer people in winter.

items.text:
Dear neighbour,
My family and I just arrived from Syria three months ago and we live in the blue house next to yours. We are happy to be your neighbours. However, there is a small problem. Your car often stays in front of our driveway at night and my husband cannot go to his early job at the bakery. Could you maybe park in front of your house? Thank you, and welcome to visit us for tea anytime.
Rania

content.text: {"refused":false,"refusalMessage":"","criteria":[{"name":"Content and task completion","strengths":"You describe the problem, its effect on your husband and a clear solution.","improve":"Mention one specific day it caused a problem."},{"name":"Organisation and coherence","strengths":"The friendly opening before the problem is a good strategy.","improve":"Add \"Kind regards,\" before your name."},{"name":"Vocabulary range and precision","strengths":"\"However, there is a small problem\" introduces the issue politely.","improve":"Remove \"maybe\" from the request; \"Could you please\" is polite enough."},{"name":"Grammar and readability","strengths":"Sentences are clear.","improve":"Check fixed phrases for invitations."}],"topErrors":[{"kind":"grammar","original":"I just arrived from Syria three months ago","correction":"I arrived from Syria three months ago","why":"\"Just\" does not fit with a finished time such as \"three months ago\"."},{"kind":"grammar","original":"welcome to visit us for tea anytime","correction":"you are welcome to visit us for tea anytime","why":"The invitation needs a subject and verb: \"you are welcome to\"."}],"rewrites":["Your car is often parked in front of our driveway at night, and my husband cannot leave for his early shift at the bakery. Could you please park in front of your own house?"],"nextStep":"Practise polite invitations and requests: \"You are welcome to ...\", \"Could you please ...\"."}

items.text: In Vietnam I worked six days every week. After I moved to Canada with Express Entry last year, I finally have normal weekends. So I choose five 8-hour days with flexible start time. Long days are very tiring, and in my experience people make more mistakes after eight hours. Flexible start also help me avoid the busy bus at 8 AM.

Flexible start times would also help me avoid the crowded bus at 8 a.m."],"nextStep":"선택을 먼저 말하고 이유를 두 가지 드는 구조로 설문 답안을 다시 써 보세요."}

items.text:
Dear Martin,
During my first winter in Canada I got sick with a strong flu, and you finished the inventory count for me without asking anything back. I was new and I did not know anyone in the company, so your kindness really made me feel part of the team. Thanks to you, the count was ready before the deadline. I would like to invite you to my home for dinner. My wife makes very good Ethiopian food!
Best,
Dawit

content.text: {"refused":false,"refusalMessage":"","criteria":[{"name":"Content and task completion","strengths":"You thank Martin, show the difference his help made, and offer dinner.","improve":"Suggest a date for the dinner to make the offer more concrete."},{"name":"Organisation and coherence","strengths":"The ideas are well connected with \"so\" and \"Thanks to you\".","improve":"Put the invitation in a separate short paragraph."},{"name":"Vocabulary range and precision","strengths":"\"Made me feel part of the team\" is warm and natural.","improve":"Check common collocations with illnesses."},{"name":"Grammar and readability","strengths":"Sentences are clear and correctly punctuated.","improve":"Keep using linking words like \"Thanks to you\" to connect ideas."}],"topErrors":[{"kind":"vocabulary","original":"a strong flu","correction":"a bad flu","why":"We say \"a bad flu\" or \"a bad cold\", not \"strong\"."},{"kind":"vocabulary","original":"without asking anything back","correction":"without asking for anything in return","why":"The natural phrase is \"without asking for anything in return\"."}],"rewrites":["During my first winter in Canada I got a bad flu, and you finished the inventory count for me without asking for anything in return."],"nextStep":"Learn five collocations with illnesses: a bad cold, a high fever, a sore throat, a mild headache, a bad flu."}

items.text: I choose bike lanes. When newcomers arrive in Canada, a car is very expensive: you need insurance, a Canadian licence and parking. My cousin came here as an international student and he rides his bike to his college and his part-time job every day. But downtown there is no safe lanes, and last year he was nearly hit by a truck. Safe bike lanes would help students and new immigrants save money and stay safe.

items.text: I prefer longer hours at public libraries. I need to reach CLB 7 in English for my Express Entry profile, so the library's quiet study room is where I practise every evening after my shift. Right now it closes at 6 PM, which is too early for workers like me. Also, the library offers free conversation circles for newcomers. With longer hours, more people could join them. Bike lanes is useful, but only in summer.

items.text: My wife and I came to Canada two years ago, she on a study permit and me on a work permit. She has classes in the morning, so I take our son to daycare. That is why I want five days with flexible start. If I work four days of ten hours, nobody can pick up our son at 5 PM. For our family, flexible time is more important than a long weekend.

items.text:
Hello,
I am your new neighbour in number 8. We immigrated from Korea in August and I started a new job that begins at 7 AM. Three times this week, a grey van was parked in front of my driveway and I was late for work. I think it belongs to your visitor. Could you please ask them to park on the street, maybe next to the park? Thank you for your understanding.
Min-jun

items.text:
Hi Luis,
Thanks a million for handling the Henderson project when I had COVID. You know how stressful the first year in a new country is, since you also immigrated from Colombia, and you understood right away that I was worry about losing this job. The client was happy and the project finished on budget. Please let me take you to the Colombian bakery on Friday, my treat!
Gratefully,
Ana

items.text: Before I immigrated, I thought Canadian cities were built only for cars. Then I discovered the library in my neighbourhood. It has free English classes, a homework club for my daughter and even a seed library. If it opened longer, more families could used these services. For these reasons, I choose longer library hours over new bike lanes.

items.text:
Dear Ms. Chen,
I joined the evening study group for the Canadian citizenship test at your centre in January. The group was cancelled after two meetings because the volunteer leader moved away. I was disappointed, since my test is in April and studying alone is harder for me. Could you please find a new leader, or give back the $25 materials fee? I would also be happy to help organize the group.
Regards,
Sadia
